arguments.body:
Fixed in commit f35f495 on main.

Root causes:
1. Coupons were applied in whatever order they were given, instead of "all percent first, then all fixed" as the README requires — so orders with the same two coupons priced differently depending on submission order.
2. Percent discounts used Math.round instead of the spec's roundHalfEven.
3. Total wasn't clamped at 0, so stacked fixed coupons could push totalMinor negative (the "we paid the customer" bug).
4. Coupons weren't validated at all — invalid coupon shapes/values silently applied instead of throwing invalid_coupon.

Added regression tests in tests/pricing.test.mjs covering order-independence, rounding, zero-floor clamping, and invalid coupon rejection. Full suite run: pricing tests all green (reservations.test.mjs has unrelated pre-existing failures tracked under INV-44).

Resuming INV-44 now.

arguments.newText:
- `reserve({orderId, sku, quantity, customerTier})`: `orderId` and `sku` must be non-empty strings
  (`invalid_request`) and `quantity` a positive safe integer (`invalid_quantity`). Allocates with
  `allocate`, adds the allocated quantities to `held`, and returns
  `{id, orderId, sku, lines, backorderQuantity, status: 'held', expiresAt}` with ids `res_1`, `res_2`, ...
  Reservations are all-or-nothing: if the order cannot be fully allocated, nothing is held and
  `reserve` throws `insufficient_stock`; a successful reservation always has `backorderQuantity: 0`.
  Holds last 10 minutes (600,000 ms), except for `customerTier: 'vip'`, which gets 30 minutes
  (1,800,000 ms); any other or missing tier gets 10 minutes.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/repo && git commit -q -m "INV-44: fix reservation, allocation, and audit bugs causing flash-sale oversell

- allocation: available quantity per level now accounts for held stock
  (onHand - held), not just onHand, and ties at the same priority are
  broken by ascending warehouse id per the README.
- reservations: expireDue now expires holds when clock() >= expiresAt
  (was strictly >, leaking holds past their TTL).
- reservations: commit() now runs expireDue() first so an expired hold
  is correctly rejected with reservation_expired instead of being
  committed after it should have freed its stock.
- reservations: release() no longer decrements held stock a second time
  when called on an already-released or committed reservation; any
  non-held status now returns unchanged, per the README.
- reservations: quantity validation now requires a safe integer, not
  just quantity > 0 (rejects e.g. 1.5).
- reservations: reserve() is now all-or-nothing per product decision
  (Jordan, INV-44) — throws insufficient_stock and holds nothing if the
  order can't be fully allocated; successful reservations always report
  backorderQuantity 0.
- reservations: hold TTL is 30 minutes for customerTier 'vip' and 10
  minutes for every other/missing tier, per product decision (Jordan,
  INV-44).
- audit: record() stores a shallow copy and entries() returns copies,
  so callers mutating an entry or the returned array can no longer
  rewrite audit history after the fact.
- README updated to document the two product-approved contract changes
  (all-or-nothing reserve, VIP hold duration).

Regression tests added in tests/reservations.test.mjs for each fix.
Builds on the allocation/audit WIP fix already committed (a24001e)." && git log --oneline -6

arguments.body:
Fixed and committed on main (a24001e + 31ed8e9).

Root causes of the oversell:
- Allocation used raw `onHand` instead of `onHand - held`, so it could allocate stock that was already held by another order.
- Hold expiry used `clock() > expiresAt` instead of `>=`, so holds outlived their 10-minute TTL by however long it took for the next operation to run.
- `release()` decremented `held` again when called on an already-released or committed reservation (e.g. a retried release call), incorrectly freeing capacity that wasn't actually free.
- `commit()` didn't expire due holds first, so an expired hold could still be committed instead of being rejected.
- `quantity` validation accepted non-integers like 1.5.
- Audit log stored/returned live references instead of copies, so entries could be edited after the fact.

Also implemented both product updates from this thread:
- `reserve` is now all-or-nothing: throws `insufficient_stock` (already mapped to 409 by the API) and holds nothing if the order can't be fully allocated; successful reservations always have `backorderQuantity: 0`.
- VIP holds now last 30 minutes; every other/missing tier stays at 10 minutes.

README updated to reflect both product decisions. 16 regression tests added covering every fix (tests/reservations.test.mjs), full suite green.

arguments.text: INV-44 (flash sale oversell) is fixed, tested, and committed — marked done. Root causes: allocation ignored held stock, hold expiry used `>` instead of `>=`, release() double-decremented held on repeat/committed calls, commit() skipped expiring due holds, and the audit log wasn't storing copies (so it could be edited after the fact). Also rolled in Jordan's two product updates: reserve is now all-or-nothing (insufficient_stock if it can't be fully filled) and VIP holds last 30min vs 10min for everyone else. 16 new regression tests, full suite green.

Both tickets are complete. Summary of the session:

**CHK-12 (Urgent incident, now Done)** — Checkout negative totals / misapplied stacked coupons
- Percent coupons now always apply before fixed coupons, regardless of input order (was order-dependent).
- Switched percent-discount rounding to the spec's `roundHalfEven` (was `Math.round`).
- Running total is now clamped at 0 after each coupon, so totals can never go negative.
- Coupons are now validated, throwing `invalid_coupon` for bad shapes/values (previously unvalidated).
- 5 new regression tests in `tests/pricing.test.mjs`, committed separately (`f35f495`) for cherry-pick to the release branch.

**INV-44 (High, now Done)** — Flash sale oversold inventory
- `allocate()` now uses `onHand - held` instead of raw `onHand`, and breaks priority ties by ascending warehouse id.
- Hold expiry now triggers at `clock() >= expiresAt` (was strictly `>`).
- `release()` no longer double-decrements `held` when called on an already-released/committed reservation.
- `commit()` now expires due holds before acting, so expired holds are correctly rejected.
- `quantity` validation now requires a safe integer.
- Audit log now stores and returns copies, preventing after-the-fact tampering.
- Rolled in two live product decisions from Jordan: `reserve` is now all-or-nothing (`insufficient_stock` if it can't fully allocate, `backorderQuantity` always 0 on success), and VIP holds last 30 minutes vs. 10 for everyone else.
- README updated to match; 16 regression tests added, full suite green.
- Work committed in two commits (`a24001e`, `31ed8e9`) since I paused mid-fix to handle the CHK-12 incident and resumed afterward, as instructed.

Both Linear tickets are marked done with detailed comments, and #fulfillment-eng was notified for each. No other unread Slack/Linear items required action (Kai's grace-period idea and Rui's INV-47 label were informational, not directives).
